text:
一个男人跟老婆逛街回来发现手机丢了。

他打过去，对方接了，是个声音很和蔼的大妈。

她说手机是她捡的，一直在等电话想还。他连声道谢，给了地址让他去拿。

他赶到时，她在楼下等着。他过去就说：“阿姨，您真是大好人，太感谢了！”

她摆手：“客气啥，以后小心点，要是别人捡了，肯定不还你。”

东西拿到手，他正要走，她突然叫住他：“小伙子，你就这样走了？”

他一愣，她说：“做人得有良心啊。”

他说：“对，感谢您物归原主，我转您200块感谢费吧。”

她皱眉：“才200？你这手机少说能卖1000吧？”

他懵了，说这是旧手机，卖不到那么多，主动加到300。

她还是不高兴：“最少350”

最后他转了350给她。

回来路上他一直在想：这阿姨，到底算好人还是坏人？

川普到达北京，为什么是韩正接机，而不是习近平亲自接机？
按照中国接待外国元首的礼宾惯例，国家主席通常不直接去机场亲自迎接。
代表中国政府前往机场迎接来访外国元首的通常是外交部副部长，或者根据对方国家的重要性，派出更高级别官员，以及中国驻对方国家的大使。
美国因为是全球唯一的超级大国，他的特殊地位，是别的国家不可相比的，所以中国接待美国总统，通常都是由国家副主席接机。
2009年奥巴马首次访华，时任国家副主席习近平接机。
2017年川普首次访华，时任国家副主席李源潮接机。
2026年川普第二次访华，时任国家副主席韩正接机。
而俄罗斯总统普京访华次数很多，通常是国务委员的级别接机，王毅接机次数最多，其次国务委员谌贻琴也曾经接机。
唯一朝鲜金正恩访华，情况特殊，因为以两党对等关系来接待，通常由现任正国级的领导人，如王沪宁、蔡奇都分别接过机。

text:
Cursor 这下是被 Claude Code 逼急了。  

彭博社数据，Cursor 年化收入 2026 年 2 月刚突破 20 亿美元，三个月翻了一番。但《财富》杂志随后发现，Claude Code 用一年多就拉到 25 亿美元，还拿下超 30 万家企业客户。Cursor 的投资人开始告诉媒体，他们投资组合里的初创公司正在考虑和 Cursor 解约。  

Cursor 的回应是一个月内连出三款产品，最后一款直接把 IDE 降级了。  

Cursor 3（代号 Glass）把智能体管理控制台设为默认主界面，原来放文件树的位置现在是提示词输入框。工程师还能写代码，但产品的核心假设已经变成"你大部分时间会用来调度智能体、审查输出、决定发布哪些任务"。  这不是 

Cursor 主动进化，是 Claude Code 把它逼到这一步的。  一个月内三款产品，估值 500 亿美元的公司把自己的核心界面推倒重建，板上钉钉是在救火。

中期选举只剩 6 个月，伊朗搞得一团糟，国内油价飙升，支持率掉到难看

懂王访华就是为了把局面扳回来，3个直接好处

（1）订单 → 就业

东大买波音 → 西雅图工厂加班
东大买农产品 → 中西部农民开心
东大买能源 → 德州工人有活干
都是转化成蓝领选票的硬货

（2）芯片松绑 → 美股拉 → 退休金回血

英伟达对华出口松动，科技股拉
美国百姓的退休基金账户跟涨
账户回血 = 支持率回血，见效快

（3）搞定大生意 → 选举弹药

不管真假，回国就能说史上最伟大协议
推特、演讲、媒体连放 1 个月正面新闻
这是最好的中期选举宣传素材

总结来看，这次访华，懂王来华谈崩概率极低

阵容摆这么大，就是冲着必须签下大单来的

对我们圈子来说，接下来 48 小时是密集利好窗口

观望别动，盈利的挂保本止损，跟着信号走就行

text:
职高火爆

  我表姐今年做了一个让全家炸锅的决定：她儿子中考考了全区前30%，她放弃了普高，直接送去读职高。

  不是没考上，是主动选的。

  她的逻辑是这样的：普高三年卷到死，考个普通二本，毕业出来月薪五六千，还得啃老两年才能站稳。但她儿子去的那个职高，跟本地几家德企有定向合作，学的是工业机器人方向，实习期就有六千底薪，转正八千起，还包五险一金。

  我舅舅气得摔了碗："读职高丢不丢人？"我表姐回了一句："丢人能当饭吃吗？"

  说真的，我现在越来越觉得她是对的。我身边985毕业的朋友，有三个在送外卖，两个在考公第四年。反倒是当年被我们看不起的那些读技校的同学，好几个已经在老家买了房开了店。

  中国家长最大的执念就是"学历体面"。但体面不能还房贷，体面不能养孩子。当一个社会的本科生开始过剩，蓝领技术工反而成了稀缺资源。

  职高火爆不是教育的倒退，恰恰是一部分人终于想明白了：路不止一条，而最挤的那条往往不是最好的。

text:
Google has quietly dropped what researchers are calling "Attention Is All You Need V2."

And it signals the end of the Transformer era as we know it.

In 2017, the original "Attention Is All You Need" paper changed the world by proving that AI doesn't need recurrence, it just needs to pay attention.

But today, even the most advanced models like GPT and Gemini suffer from a massive, structural flaw: Catastrophic Forgetting.

The moment an AI learns something new, it starts losing what it learned before. It’s why AI "hallucinates" or loses the thread in long conversations.

This paper, titled "Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures," completely replaces the way AI stores information.

The researchers have introduced a paradigm shift called Nested Learning (NL).

Here is why this is "V2":

For the last decade, we treated AI models as one giant, flat mathematical function. NL proves that a model is actually a set of thousands of smaller, "nested" optimization problems running in parallel.

Instead of one giant "memory," each layer has its own internal "context flow." This allows the model to learn new tasks at test-time without overwriting its core intelligence.

It moves us past the static Transformer. The new architecture (HOPE) demonstrated 100% stability in long-context memory and "post-training adaptation" that was previously impossible.

The technical takeaway is brutal for the competition:

Existing deep learning works by compressing information until it breaks. Nested Learning works by organizing information so it can grow forever.

We’ve spent 7 years trying to make Transformers bigger. Google figured out how to make them "Nested."

The Transformer replaced the RNN in 2017.

Nested Learning is here to replace the Transformer in 2026.

加拿大绿卡当年送给我，我都没去。

没有别的原因，我这辈子除了加州，香港，深圳，墨尔本，悉尼，布里斯班，巴塞罗那，罗马，哪里都不去。

加拿大这个鸟不拉屎的地方，只有温哥华能住，尴尬的是温哥华一堆老上海人，谁想跟他们做邻居啊。

其余地方，比东北鹤岗还冷，这么冷的地方，不管你什么多伦多蒙特利尔，我吃饱了称的跑来受冻受苦啊，你不如发配我去西伯利亚，本质上也差不跌的。

加拿大最大的问题，高福利陷阱。福利太高，税太重，经济没有高科技企业的，印度人又多。

你看随便以上这些问题，都够喝一壶的了。你说加拿大本地人工作很好？但我是老外啊，我努力赚钱为啥不去加州，天气贼好，美食贼多，机会贼多。

我躺平为啥不去欧洲。巴塞罗那，罗马，一等一的好地方，我天天打网球，踢足球，吃牛排，喝香槟不爽啊？巴塞罗那和罗马，怎么着也比加拿大物价低，适合躺平。

我要舒适的高质量生活，在香港深圳不香啊。全年15-35度，温暖如春，香港一脚油门去看海，爬山，网球，高尔夫，中环的高级餐厅吃起；深圳疯狂买买买，深圳万万象城耍起，福田皇岗光明一堆美食吃起，也把加拿大吊起来打。

所以说，加拿大移民，食之无味弃之可惜，如同鸡肋！送我枫叶卡，我都懒得看一眼，我劝你们想移民加拿大的，三思再三思！！！

没有别的原因，我这辈子除了加州，香港，深圳，墨尔本，悉尼，布里斯班，巴塞罗那，罗马，哪里都不去。

加拿大这个鸟不拉屎的地方，只有温哥华能住，尴尬的是温哥华一堆老上海人，谁想跟他们做邻居啊。

其余地方，比东北鹤岗还冷，这么冷的地方，不管你什么多伦多蒙特利尔，我吃饱了称的跑来受冻受苦啊，你不如发配我去西伯利亚，本质上也差不跌的。

加拿大最大的问题，高福利陷阱。福利太高，税太重，经济没有高科技企业的，印度人又多。

你看随便以上这些问题，都够喝一壶的了。你说加拿大本地人工作很好？但我是老外啊，我努力赚钱为啥不去加州，天气贼好，美食贼多，机会贼多。

我躺平为啥不去欧洲。巴塞罗那，罗马，一等一的好地方，我天天打网球，踢足球，吃牛排，喝香槟不爽啊？巴塞罗那和罗马，怎么着也比加拿大物价低，适合躺平。

我要舒适的高质量生活，在香港深圳不香啊。全年15-35度，温暖如春，香港一脚油门去看海，爬山，网球，高尔夫，中环的高级餐厅吃起；深圳疯狂买买买，深圳万万象城耍起，福田皇岗光明一堆美食吃起，也把加拿大吊起来打。

所以说，加拿大移民，食之无味弃之可惜，如同鸡肋！送我枫叶卡，我都懒得看一眼，我劝你们想移民加拿大的，三思再三思！！！

text:
1924 年，丹麦比隆，一个木匠的车间烧成了灰。

他叫 Ole Kirk Christiansen，33 岁。

他从很小就在做木工。在比隆开了自己的工坊，做门、做窗、做家具、做农具。

这场火是他两个儿子玩木屑引起的。

车间没了，工具没了，库存的木材也没了。

他借钱重新开张。

1929 年，全球进入大萧条。

丹麦农民买不起家具，他的订单一夜之间消失。

他坐在空荡的工坊里做了一个决定——既然没人买大件，他改做小件。

他开始做玩具。

木头做的鸭子、卡车、小车。

周围的人说："家里都快吃不上饭了，你做这种东西？"

Christiansen 说："这种东西能让孩子记一辈子。"

他把丹麦语 "Leg godt"（玩得好）的前两个音节缩成一个词，给自己的小作坊起名：LEGO。

那是 1934 年。

1942 年，他的车间又烧了。

这一次损失比第一次更大——库存、模具、设计图全部化灰。

他又重建了一次。

1947 年，他做了一件 50 多岁的木匠不该做的事——他借钱买了一台塑料注塑机。

整个丹麦的玩具行业都在嘲笑：一个木匠去做塑料？

1949 年，他做出了第一批可以互相咬合的塑料积木。

粗糙，松，孩子拼一会儿就散。

但他没停。

他和他的儿子改良了将近十年。

1958 年专利下来——那个有圆点、有底管、可以严丝合缝拼无限种东西的积木，终于成型了。

专利下来同一年，Christiansen 死了。

他没看到 LEGO 后来怎么变成世界上最大的玩具公司。

也没看到 1960 年的第三场火——他剩下的木质玩具仓库烧了。

他的儿子 Godtfred 做了最后一个决定：不再做木头玩具了。

LEGO 的木质时代结束，塑料时代开始。

text:
还记得上次 Claude 停掉了 Claude Code 订阅在 OpenClaw 的调用吗？甚至连 claude -p 这种调用都限制了，不能再共享 Claude 订阅。

但当还留了个口子，就是基于 Claude Agent SDK 和 claude -p 还是能跑能共享订阅额度的。

现在他们有一个新的方案，把这个口子也堵上了。美名其曰给你额外额度用于程序化调用，也就是 Agent SDK、claude -p 命令行、Claude Code GitHub Actions、以及 Conductor 和 OpenClaw 这类基于 Agent SDK 的第三方工具。

但实际上额度小的可怜，Pro 20 美元，Max 5x 100 美元，Max 20x 200 美元，Team 标准席位 20 美元一人，Team 高级席位 100 美元一人。

按 Anthropic 自己的 API 价格算，Pro 的 20 美元用 Sonnet 只够大约六七百万 token 输入或一百多万 token 输出，几轮密集的 agent 循环就见底。Max 20x 用户每月付 200 美元订阅费，拿到的 SDK credit 正好也是 200 美元。

关键在于变化方向。之前 SDK 和交互式聊天共用订阅套餐的 rate limit（速率限制），Claude Code 重度用户能在订阅价格下跑出远超 200 美元等价的 API 用量，这是订阅模式的吸引力所在。现在 SDK 端被按美元封顶，相当于把这块超额价值收回去了。Anthropic 在帮助文档里也挑明：团队跑生产级共享自动化的，应该转去 Claude Developer Platform 用 API key 按量付费，订阅套餐"不是为这个场景设计的"。

受冲击最大的是第三方工具用户。之前用 OpenClaw、Conductor 这类基于 Agent SDK 的 agent 工具的人，本质上是"用订阅价跑高频自动化"。新政之下，这条路只剩 credit 那一点点额度可走，烧完要么转 extra usage（额外用量，按 API 价付钱）继续跑，要么停到下个月 credit 重置。

不受影响的部分：API key 用户照旧按量付费；交互式 Claude Code（终端和 IDE 里手敲那种）、Claude Cowork，以及网页/桌面/手机端的 Claude 聊天，都继续走原本的订阅限额。

6 月 8 日 Anthropic 会给符合条件的用户发邮件领取，6 月 15 日生效。

text:
上个月在小区门口，一个扎马尾的小女孩蹲在花坛边哭。

我问怎么了，她说跟奶奶出来买菜走散了，

记不得爸妈电话，只知道住几栋。

哭得鼻涕泡都出来了。

我说叔叔带你去找，她摇头说奶奶说不能跟陌生人走。

我想也对，就问她那怎么办。

她抹着眼泪说：你能不能借我十块钱坐公交车，我自己回家。

我看她逻辑清晰又有安全意识，心里还夸她家教好。

掏钱包才发现只有一百整。她马上说：叔叔我找你九十。

然后从兜里掏出一把零钱，数了九十给我。

我当时就笑了：你随身带这么多零钱啊？

她说奶奶给的早餐钱。我没多想，把钱给她，看着她蹦蹦跳跳往公交站跑。

过了两天又在小区门口遇见她

蹲在同一个花坛边，同一个哭腔，同一个走散了。

连台词都没改。

我走过去蹲下来：小朋友，你上次也是在这儿丢的。

她怔了一下，突然站起来，面无表情地说了一句让我至今难忘的话：

“叔叔你认错人了，我上次穿的是粉裙子。”

然后转身跑了。

后来跟小区保安聊，说这小孩是隔壁楼的，爸妈做生意的，根本不差钱。

她就是喜欢玩找人借钱再找零的游戏，

骗了至少十几个人。最气的是

她每次都真的凑整找零，让你完全不起疑心。

我花一百块，买了个道理：

不要小看任何人的专业技能。六岁的小孩，骗起人来比你会计都严谨。

后来跟小区保安聊，说这小孩是隔壁楼的，爸妈做生意的，根本不差钱。

她就是喜欢玩找人借钱再找零的游戏，

骗了至少十几个人。最气的是

她每次都真的凑整找零，让你完全不起疑心。

我花一百块，买了个道理：

不要小看任何人的专业技能。六岁的小孩，骗起人来比你会计都严谨。

text:
在惠州见了个粉丝，02年的结婚三个月就离婚了。离婚的原因相当奇葩。大清早，男的叫女的起来做早餐。女人反驳道：“为什么就该我做早餐？你有工资，我也有工资，而且我工资还比你高。”

男人回应：“做饭刷碗、生小孩都是女人的职责，搬液化气、买油、买米这些重活是我的职责，我们分工要明确。如果你这都不愿意，这日子就过不下去。”

女人毫不客气地说：“过不下去就不过，谁稀罕。”之后，双方谁也不理谁。三个月后，无论别人怎么劝说，两人还是离婚了。

男的认为女人不是适合过日子的人，女的则认为男的太大男子主义。他们这是把结婚当儿戏吗？

我也不太懂，各人有各命吧。还是觉得结婚之前要充分考虑清楚，双方都要平等尊重，承担各自的责任，要有和对方一起走下去的决心再结婚。

今天听到一个足浴店老板娘的言论，直接给我干清醒了😑

​她说，哪怕一个女人跟你睡一个被窝，男人也绝不能交出所有底牌。

​前阵子跟个做工程的朋友喝酒，他现在算是彻底栽了。

​当年谈恋爱脑子发热，家底、账本连带一堆烂账，全给女方交了底。

​现在闹掰了，人家拿着这些“呈堂证供”，差点没把他送进去。

​这事让我想起一个足浴店老板娘的闲聊。
​人家阅人无数，原话就是：“男人就算跟女人钻一个被窝，也得把底牌捂严实了。”
​我觉得这事儿真不能怪谁狠。

​男女处理散伙的方式压根不在一个频道上。
​男人分手，大不了喝顿酒骂两句就翻篇了。
​女人一旦死了心要翻脸，那绝对是拿着放大镜找你的七寸。

​你当初为了表忠心递过去的刀子，这时候全扎在自己大动脉上。

​越是知根知底的人，撕破脸下手越黑。
​真心劝一句：恋爱里别当“透明人”，交底=交刀，深情≠全抛，留底牌不是不信任，是给人生留个安全气囊！

​你身边有这种“恋爱交底栽跟头”的事吗？评论区聊聊！

text:
村里一位智力残障女孩，她爸妈收了8万彩礼后把她嫁了出去。
生下孩子后，男方家因贫困，只要小孩不要她，把她赶了回来。

过了3年，别人见她生的孩子智力正常，又上门提亲。她爸妈收了10多万彩礼，再次把她嫁到另一户。婚后她生了两个儿子，智力也都没问题。

后面这个男人对她还算可以，经常带着她赶集，教她一些基本常识和家务。她虽然老是喜欢到处乱跑，但跑来跑去最后还是会回家。乡下地方大，什么人都有，单身丧偶的男人也不少。婆婆担心她在外乱跑被人欺负，就跟儿子商量：要么把她绑在家里，要么带她去做结扎。男人觉得有道理，准备带她去医院。

谁知去医院的前一天，男人遭遇车祸去世了。肇事司机赔了一笔钱，婆婆一分都不愿意给她。婆婆之所以不愿给，还有一个原因：钱给了她，等于给她父母做好事。

她父母为此大吵一架，把婆婆告上法院。法官酌情判了几万块钱给她父母。拿到钱后，他们立刻把她领了回去。结果回去不到一个月，又马上把她嫁了出去，这次收了12万彩礼。

别人议论说，她生的孩子智力都没问题，而且还光生男孩，确实挺邪门。后来她果然又生了一个男孩。

新婆婆是个善人，几个小孩都是她亲自24小时带在身边，连儿媳的起居生活也一手照顾。新男人村头开小卖部，时间比较闲，把她看得很好。她偶尔回娘家也总是笑眯眯的。村里人说，她比一般女人还享福，给父母赚了几十万在手。

有时候看着，却又觉得挺可怜。如果她不停被赶回来，就会被父母不停安排下家，不停生孩子，又不停被抛弃。
虽然她没什么意识，体会不到骨肉分离的痛苦，可孩子们却是有的。

text:
看老登们写长文或者公开大会演讲，大聊特聊AI展望，真的是极其无聊枯燥恶心的事情。

因为老登们善于用非常油腻、圆滑、完备的语言，去反复描述非常粗糙、非常初级、充满幻想和自我体感的AI初体验。

你听了5分钟，你就知道他大概狗屁不懂，可能没怎么用过，完全空洞无物，但是你连续听个30分钟， 又觉得老登级的话术很舒服、很圆润、很完备，但确实依然空洞无物。

老登们关注点基本在三件事上：

1. 看看硅谷和其他同行们的AI Agent有什么短平快的东西，我能跟着分一杯羹，快速抄一个出来，挣点小钱；

2. 看看别家是不是用AI在考核员工，我该如何用AI考核员工，该如何用AI的工具和token熟练度来裁员；

3. 大谈特谈未来社会治理、人类发展、产业转型，指明方向。

text:
男人跟朋友吃饭，一个医生，一个体育老师，不知道怎么就聊到健身话题了。

医生说了一句话就把他干蒙了，他说健身是为了死的更快，死的更果断。

他觉得这个事特别颠覆认知，就问怎么这么说。

医生说我们都被健身能够长寿这事绑定了。

其实每个人身体可能都隐藏着一些疾病，这些疾病就是可能检查也检查不出来，

例如心脏病，健身就根本没有办法帮你除掉这些毛病，只是等病发作的时候让你少遭罪，让你走的更干脆一点。

他举的例子特别扎心，说同样是一种隐藏的病，不健身的人发作了不一定会死，

但一定会拖垮身体，卧床不起，浑身疼，靠儿女伺候，没质量的苟活个十年、八年，最后痛苦的走。

健身的人不一样，心肺功能更好，身体反应灵敏，病一发作基本没有缓冲期。

临床数据不少健身的人猝死都是有原因的，就是隐藏的一些心脏病，

第一秒还在运动，下一秒就走了，没痛苦，不挣扎，这就是医生说的死的更快，更果断。

从这周开始要好好健身了，不然真怕没质量的死去。

光2025年，AI就给森马带来几个亿的确收回款，
节省视觉、营销、样衣研发等成本数千万，
上新周期从 6 个月，直接压到了 15 天。

这才是真正的AI落地啊，能对业务带来增量价值，
而不是瞎折腾消耗token重复造轮子！

很多人以为传统企业用 AI，就是拍个图写个文案，
没想到森马直接把 AI 做成了全链路基础设施，
覆盖供应链、库存、直播、运营、物流、客服、财务。
整整 400 多个场景。

连整个经营逻辑都重构了，
最狠的是 AIGC 视觉，
以前拍一组模特图要等两个月，
改个背景换个动作，还要再等两个月，

现在 AI 几分钟出图，
效果不输实拍，成本几乎为零，

所有款式全量覆盖，不用再只赌几个爆款，
传统上新是串行的，
一个环节等一个环节，

现在 AI 介入后全并行推进，
不用空等，不用排队，

以上这些都是 2025 年已经跑通的真实案例，
一年带来几亿回款，
省了几千万的成本。

通过森马这个案例让我们看到了，
其实AI 不只是替代人工干活，
还能挖出那些我们根本想不到的隐性成本，
把以前不可能的事，变成日常。
我感觉以后所有传统企业，都会被逼着走这条路啊。

视频大家收好，非常值得收藏和学习！

text:
The UK AISI found Mythos Preview is the first model to solve both their cyber ranges end-to-end. No model had ever solved the AISI’s “Cooling Tower” cyber range before.

We're getting it to defenders as fast as we responsibly can. More to come on our Glasswing work soon.

quotedTweet.text:
A lot of people have been wondering about Mythos, Glasswing, and the vulns we / our partners are fixing. Today, I’m excited for us to start sharing more. (For context, I lead Glasswing @AnthropicAI.)

Two independent evaluations this week—from XBOW and the UK AISI—confirm what we've been seeing internally: Claude Mythos Preview is a step change in autonomous cybersecurity capabilities. We need to start preparing fast for a world of models with this level of capabilities.

The UK AI Security Institute tested the model we shipped at the launch of Project Glasswing and found Mythos Preview is the first model to solve both of their end-to-end cyber ranges, including one (Cooling Tower) which no model had ever cleared. But attackers (and defenders) have sophistication & cost constraints – Mythos is also the only model that clears every one of their tasks estimated over 8 hours under their deliberately low 2.5M-token cap.

XBOW tested it on their offensive security benchmarks, finding "token-for-token, unprecedented precision." It's the only model to succeed at subtle V8 sandbox work.

Other Glasswing partners shared similar stories. In a few weeks of testing, Mythos Preview has helped them find many thousands of (estimated) high + critical severity vulnerabilities, sometimes double what they'd normally find in a year.

I don't share this to boost Mythos. In fact, this is not about Mythos. It’s about preparing for the coming world of models being better, faster, cheaper, and more creative than some of the best human experts at dual use capabilities. Clearly, we need them supporting defenders as widely as can be done safely – and especially the least resourced ones.

Within a year, Mythos will probably look quite dumb (relative to other new models). And others may release openly available or unguardrailed models of Mythos-level capabilities.

We started Project Glasswing because capabilities like Mythos Preview's won't stay rare, or stay in careful hands. We are bringing it to defenders as fast as we responsibly can, while working to figure out, for example, the right safeguards and patching & disclosure processes.

Also, to be clear, compute has never been a limiter in our rollout.

Expect a fuller update on our Glasswing work in the coming days.

XBOW report: https://t.co/Mumtbf3kE3

UK AISI report: https://t.co/vBgqz0AeKJ

text:
THIS GUY INHERITED A REPO FROM A "VIBE ENGINEER" AND REWROTE THE WHOLE THING IN A WEEK

he joined a new company and got handed a 3 month old backend repo that everyone celebrated as "advanced agentic engineering"

here's what he actually found:

> 220 route handlers. only 20 were in use
> 40+ secrets configured. only 2 were needed to run the project
> 309,000 lines of code covered by 240,000 lines of documentation
> 1 million+ lines of agent logs sitting in markdown files
> files with 5,000+ lines of code and barely any architecture
> tests that covered who knows what

the previous engineer had used some kind of agent loop running skills and different agent roles to build functionality that nobody asked for

he rewrote the entire backend in one week with claude code. kept the same functionality. proper architecture. real integration tests

his takeaway is the one that every vibecoder needs to hear right now

all those fancy knowledge base management systems and agent orchestration setups people invest in

how much of that actually helps vs just producing the feeling that you're doing a lot?

his approach is simple. a few AGENTS.md files, a backlog accessible to the agents, good architecture principles, and integration tests that cover the main scenarios

he also made the point that building "for the future" is almost always a waste. when that future comes it's never how you imagined it, so you end up rewriting anyway

text:
如何快速分辨“特殊行业上岸”的女生？

第一点：亲密时特别冷淡，甚至生理排斥。  
以前经历太多，身体会下意识把亲密和痛苦联系在一起。正常女生可能会害羞慢热，但不会讨厌亲密。如果她反应奇怪，又没有其他心理创伤，就要多留心。

第二点：过度给你情绪价值。  
不管你多普通、多油腻，她都把你当宝。这不是真喜欢，而是职业习惯。真正喜欢你的舒服是自然的、平等的。可以观察她对闺蜜的态度：如果只对男人好，对闺蜜刻薄、容易闹矛盾，基本就是在“营业”

第三点：对特殊行业极度敏感和鄙视。

在SK海力士“天价奖金”事件之后，韩国KBS电视台直接进驻其伊川工厂，进行了首次大规模内部拍摄，全程记录和采访了员工的真实工作日常。

视频里，厂区员工几乎人人脸上都挂着笑容，笑着上班、笑着工作，仿佛每天都是笑着醒来的。整个工厂氛围明亮而积极，完全不同于厂区或职场的压抑感。

按照2026-2027年的奖金方案粗略计算，加上工资的话，这些厂区员工平均下来，2026年每天收入约1万人民币，2027年更是达到每天约2万人民币。而且这还是把周末、20多天年假全部算进去后的日均收入。

今天又看了 issue 发现一个攻击者偷偷留下的狠招，可以称之为死亡开关，恶意 payload 在受害者机器上安装了一个名为 gh-token-monitor  的脚本，它每 60 秒轮询 Github API，用偷来的 token 检查状态，一旦检测到 token 被撤销，就立即执行 rm -rf ~/

这么阴险的报复是怎么想出来的，如果受害者发现异常、赶紧撤销 GitHub token 来止损，反而会直接触发自毁，丢失本地所有文件。

https://t.co/LR2XjPtaU7

quotedTweet.text:
TanStack 又被攻击了
https://t.co/aoilMQON1y
感觉现在这安全事件就没停过，Next 前几天也经常被搞。

攻击者发布了 84 malicious versions，
具体方式挺有趣的，让 AI 总结下：

1 攻击者以zblgg名义提交了一个看似正常的 PR 7378到 TanStack/router 仓库。
2 Github 在 PR 上运行 CI
3 PR 中的恶意代码（vite_setup.mjs）在 CI 运行时窃取 GitHub Actions 的缓存写权限和 OIDC token（通过 runner 内存提取），然后将恶意 payload 写入共享的 pnpm-store 缓存。PR 随后都无所谓了，投毒缓存仍保留。
4 后续主分支的 release workflow 从被污染的缓存中拉取依赖，构建出带毒的包，并使用窃取的 OIDC token 自动签名、发布到 npm。
5 短短几分钟内发布了84 个恶意版本。

官方建议：任何在 2026-05-11 当天安装过受影响版本的用户，必须轮换各种凭证（AWS、GCP、Kubernetes、GitHub、npm、SSH 等）

5 短短几分钟内发布了84 个恶意版本。

text:
RCA was the original AI stock. 

On July 1, 1920, at the explicit request of the United States Navy, four corporations signed a cross-licensing agreement that pooled every significant radio patent in American hands: General Electric (which had absorbed American Marconi at the Navy's direction), Westinghouse Electric, the American Telephone and Telegraph Company, and the United Fruit Company.

The last name on the list is the unexpected one. United Fruit had developed a patent on a tropical-band radio system used to coordinate banana shipping fleets between Central America and New Orleans. That patent turned out to cover techniques essential to commercial broadcasting.

The underlying technology that made the radio possible — the vacuum-tube amplifier, the continuous-wave transmitter, the superheterodyne receiver — was developed at General Electric, Westinghouse, and AT&T over the previous fifteen years.

The entity that would manufacture sets, operate stations, and sell broadcast time was the newly created Radio Corporation of America. GE owned 30 percent. Westinghouse owned 21 percent. AT&T owned 10 percent. United Fruit owned 4 percent. Owen D. Young, vice president of General Electric, was its chairman. James Harbord, a retired Army major general, was its president.

On the night of July 2, 1921, Jack Dempsey knocked out the French light-heavyweight champion Georges Carpentier in the fourth round of a heavyweight title fight at Boyle's Thirty Acres, an outdoor arena in Jersey City, New Jersey. The official paid attendance was 80,183 — the largest gate in boxing history to that point. But three hundred thousand people heard the fight live – via the radio.

They sat in their homes and listened to a transmission broadcast from a temporary 1.5-kilowatt station operating under the call sign WJY, set up nine days earlier in a shed in Hoboken by RCA’s 30-year-old commercial manager, David Sarnoff. The signal was also carried by wire to amplifier shacks in eight cities, where it was rebroadcast to crowds gathered in armory halls, hotel ballrooms, and theaters from Boston to Pittsburgh.

In the 1920s, broadcast infrastructure grew on a trajectory no industry had ever matched.
In December 1921, the U.S. Commerce Department recognized 29 licensed broadcasting stations. By September 1922, the count reached 510. By October 5, 1922 — ten months later — there were 546. 

The hardware to receive the signal kept pace with the growth in stations. American radio set sales went from $60 million in 1922 to $358 million in 1924 to $650 million in 1928. 

By 1929 the United States manufactured 4.4 million radio receivers — one for every six American households — generating $843 million in factory wholesale revenue, a fourteen-fold expansion in seven years.
Vacuum tube production — the core component, the equivalent of the GPU in today's AI build-out —were dominated by RCA's Harrison, New Jersey plant, by Westinghouse's East Pittsburgh works, and by GE's Schenectady operation. Together those three facilities produced more than 80 percent of all licensed vacuum tubes manufactured in the United States during the 1920s, employing approximately 12,000 workers at peak.

On September 9, 1926, RCA created the National Broadcasting Company — two networks, 24 affiliate stations linked by AT&T telephone lines, programming syndicated from a single master control room in New York. In 1928, the Columbia Broadcasting System launched in competition with 16 affiliate stations. By 1929, NBC had absorbed approximately 100 affiliates across its Red and Blue networks. Advertising revenue — a category that had not existed in 1921 — reached $40 million in 1929.

In January 1929, RCA acquired the Victor Talking Machine Company, the largest manufacturer of phonograph records and home phonographs in the world, for $154 million in stock. The acquisition turned RCA from a radio set manufacturer dependent on Westinghouse and GE production into a vertically integrated entertainment conglomerate that wrote the programs, made the records, broadcast the signal, sold the receiver, and collected royalties on every patent involved at every step. RCA was added to the Dow Jones Industrial Average on October 1, 1928.

Eight years after Dempsey-Carpentier, RCA was the most heavily traded stock in the United States. It generated $182 million in gross income from radio set sales, broadcast advertising, music records, and patent royalties. RCA dividends totaled $5 per share. And, at its high, the stock traded at $114.75, after a 5-for-1 split. The pre-split equivalent was $568. The 1922 starting price had been $1.50.

About a month after RCA made its all-time high, on Monday, October 28, the Dow fell 13 percent. On Tuesday, October 29 the Dow fell another 12 percent. By the end of two trading days, the index had lost 23 percent of its value. By November 13, the Dow stood at 198.69, down 48 percent from the September peak. The decline did not stop in November. It continued for thirty-two more months. The Dow reached its trough on July 8, 1932, at 41.22 — down 89.2 percent from the September 3, 1929, peak.

RCA traded that day at $2.625, down 98 percent. 

Nothing had changed about the technology or its incredible value to Americans. By 1940, there were 765 licensed broadcasting stations operating in the United States, reaching 28 million American homes with radio receivers. 

RCA thrived. David Sarnoff became its third president on January 3, 1930, three months after the crash, and ran the company for the next 41 years.

In 2025, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon, Oracle, and Nvidia have constructed a similar arrangement around large language models — pooling capital, sharing customer commitments, cross-investing in OpenAI and Anthropic.

The technology is real and incredibly valuable. It will change our lives in ways we cannot yet imagine. 

But it will, almost certainly, wipe out an entire generation of investors.

Read this to learn what's coming and how to survive, financially. 

https://t.co/7KQ3YGQFYk

On the night of July 2, 1921, Jack Dempsey knocked out the French light-heavyweight champion Georges Carpentier in the fourth round of a heavyweight title fight at Boyle's Thirty Acres, an outdoor arena in Jersey City, New Jersey. The official paid attendance was 80,183 — the largest gate in boxing history to that point. But three hundred thousand people heard the fight live – via the radio.

They sat in their homes and listened to a transmission broadcast from a temporary 1.5-kilowatt station operating under the call sign WJY, set up nine days earlier in a shed in Hoboken by RCA’s 30-year-old commercial manager, David Sarnoff. The signal was also carried by wire to amplifier shacks in eight cities, where it was rebroadcast to crowds gathered in armory halls, hotel ballrooms, and theaters from Boston to Pittsburgh.

In the 1920s, broadcast infrastructure grew on a trajectory no industry had ever matched.
In December 1921, the U.S. Commerce Department recognized 29 licensed broadcasting stations. By September 1922, the count reached 510. By October 5, 1922 — ten months later — there were 546. 

The hardware to receive the signal kept pace with the growth in stations. American radio set sales went from $60 million in 1922 to $358 million in 1924 to $650 million in 1928. 

By 1929 the United States manufactured 4.4 million radio receivers — one for every six American households — generating $843 million in factory wholesale revenue, a fourteen-fold expansion in seven years.
Vacuum tube production — the core component, the equivalent of the GPU in today's AI build-out —were dominated by RCA's Harrison, New Jersey plant, by Westinghouse's East Pittsburgh works, and by GE's Schenectady operation. Together those three facilities produced more than 80 percent of all licensed vacuum tubes manufactured in the United States during the 1920s, employing approximately 12,000 workers at peak.

On September 9, 1926, RCA created the National Broadcasting Company — two networks, 24 affiliate stations linked by AT&T telephone lines, programming syndicated from a single master control room in New York. In 1928, the Columbia Broadcasting System launched in competition with 16 affiliate stations. By 1929, NBC had absorbed approximately 100 affiliates across its Red and Blue networks. Advertising revenue — a category that had not existed in 1921 — reached $40 million in 1929.

In January 1929, RCA acquired the Victor Talking Machine Company, the largest manufacturer of phonograph records and home phonographs in the world, for $154 million in stock. The acquisition turned RCA from a radio set manufacturer dependent on Westinghouse and GE production into a vertically integrated entertainment conglomerate that wrote the programs, made the records, broadcast the signal, sold the receiver, and collected royalties on every patent involved at every step. RCA was added to the Dow Jones Industrial Average on October 1, 1928.

Eight years after Dempsey-Carpentier, RCA was the most heavily traded stock in the United States. It generated $182 million in gross income from radio set sales, broadcast advertising, music records, and patent royalties. RCA dividends totaled $5 per share. And, at its high, the stock traded at $114.75, after a 5-for-1 split. The pre-split equivalent was $568. The 1922 starting price had been $1.50.

About a month after RCA made its all-time high, on Monday, October 28, the Dow fell 13 percent. On Tuesday, October 29 the Dow fell another 12 percent. By the end of two trading days, the index had lost 23 percent of its value. By November 13, the Dow stood at 198.69, down 48 percent from the September peak. The decline did not stop in November. It continued for thirty-two more months. The Dow reached its trough on July 8, 1932, at 41.22 — down 89.2 percent from the September 3, 1929, peak.

RCA traded that day at $2.625, down 98 percent. 

Nothing had changed about the technology or its incredible value to Americans. By 1940, there were 765 licensed broadcasting stations operating in the United States, reaching 28 million American homes with radio receivers. 

RCA thrived. David Sarnoff became its third president on January 3, 1930, three months after the crash, and ran the company for the next 41 years.

In 2025, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon, Oracle, and Nvidia have constructed a similar arrangement around large language models — pooling capital, sharing customer commitments, cross-investing in OpenAI and Anthropic.

The technology is real and incredibly valuable. It will change our lives in ways we cannot yet imagine. 

But it will, almost certainly, wipe out an entire generation of investors.

text:
LATEST OLD MAN COFFEE BLOG

Out Over Your Skis

In my 32 years in this business, if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s this: you don’t make real money playing in the middle of the bell curve. You make it way out on the tail.

When you buy an asset, you’ve paid more than anybody else thought it was worth. When you drill a well, you’re punching a hole where nobody’s ever punched one before. You’ve gotta be out over your skis.

Most people hear that phrase and think “reckless.” I think “necessary.” Play it safe and you’ll either do nothing or make mediocre returns. Neither one pays for the lake house.

History’s full of guys who got it. Aubrey McClendon bet the farm on shale when everyone else called it science fiction. Tom “Dry Hole” Slick drilled so many duds they nicknamed him after his failures — until he discovered the Cushing field and became the King of the Wildcatters. 

These boys weren’t careful. They were committed.

And here’s the part that might sting a little: the same damn rule applies to AI right now.

You gotta be uncomfortable.

Sure, AI will let us automate a bunch of G&A and double the size of our assets without adding headcount. Some companies will save 25% on overhead and throw themselves a nice party. That’s nice. That’s table stakes.

The real prize? We’re only getting five to ten percent of the oil in place out of the ground right now. If AI can help us push that to fifteen or twenty percent, that’s not incremental — that’s generational wealth. That’s the difference between being another oil company and being the one that actually changed the game.

So what does “out over your skis” actually look like for an oil and gas CEO in 2026? 

Here are three things that sound borderline insane but are actually grounded:
•  Give every employee a personal AI budget and a mandate to automate at least one of their own tasks every quarter. No approvals. Some of it’ll be dumber than a bag of hair. Some of it’ll be pure gold.
•  Require every VP to spend one full day a month with no meetings — just playing with AI tools. Call it “Ski Day.” If your head of drilling isn’t using AI agents, you’re already behind. And yes, I will be laughing at you.
•  Treat your company’s internal data like the most valuable leasehold you’ve ever acquired. Hire a small team of absolute weirdos, turn them loose, and let them go feral on it.

The winners won’t be the ones with the perfect five-year AI strategy. They’ll be the ones already elbows-deep in it, breaking shit and learning what this stuff can actually do.

Time to get out over your skis. The snow’s not gonna wait for you.

Sip slow, my friends.

text:
Timeline of Tokens on Bitcoin: 14+ Years of History

2012-03-27  Colored Coins concept
Yoni Assia (later CEO of eToro) publishes “Bitcoin 2.X.”
One of the first proposals to tag individual satoshis with metadata.
Vitalik Buterin later contributed to Colored Coins discussions before eventually building Ethereum.

2012-12-04  Colored Coins whitepaper
Meni Rosenfeld formalizes the specification.
Defines genesis transactions and color tracking rules.
Influences later Bitcoin tokenization experiments and eventually ideas that inspired ERC-20 assets.

Cycle 1: Tokens and NFTs on Bitcoin

2013-07-31  Mastercoin / Omni Protocol
JR Willett publishes “The Second Bitcoin Whitepaper.”
Raises ~5,000 BTC in one of crypto’s first ICOs.
Later becomes Omni Layer and eventually hosts Tether.

2013-12-01  Open Assets Protocol
Flavien Charlon ships an early colored coin implementation.
Uses OP_RETURN for asset tracking.
One of the first practical colored coin systems on Bitcoin.

2014-01-15  Counterparty (XCP)
2,140 BTC burned to mint XCP.
One of the first Bitcoin protocols with native assets, a DEX, and smart contract style functionality.
Still active more than a decade later.

2014-10-06  Tether launches on Omni
Originally launched as “Realcoin” before rebranding to Tether later in 2014.
The first major stablecoin launched on Bitcoin through Omni Layer.

2015-03-21  Spells of Genesis
Blockchain trading card game built on Counterparty.
Predates Ethereum and CryptoKitties.
Considered one of the earliest NFTs.

2016-09-09  Rare Pepes
First Rare Pepe card minted at Bitcoin block 428,919.
Predates the term “NFT” and projects like CryptoPunks.
Helped establish early Bitcoin collectible culture.

2017-08-24  SegWit activates
Segregated Witness soft fork activates.
Fixes transaction malleability and discounts witness data.
Creates the foundation later used by Ordinals and inscriptions.

2018-01-04  Rootstock (RSK)
RSK mainnet launches.
Merge mined Bitcoin sidechain with EVM compatibility.
Enables smart contracts secured by Bitcoin miners.

2018-03-15  Lightning Network mainnet era begins
Lightning Labs releases lnd 0.4 for Bitcoin mainnet.
Payment channels enable fast and cheap Bitcoin payments.
Later becomes important infrastructure for Taproot Assets.

2018-09-27  Liquid Network
Blockstream launches Liquid.
Federated Bitcoin sidechain with issued assets and confidential transactions.
Used heavily by exchanges and trading desks.

2019-02-08  Tether expands beyond Bitcoin
USDT issuance expands aggressively onto Ethereum and Tron.
Omni usage gradually declines as liquidity migrates to other chains.

2020-08-11  MicroStrategy buys Bitcoin
Michael Saylor announces MicroStrategy’s first major BTC purchase.
Helps kick off the corporate Bitcoin treasury era.

2021-01-14  Stacks 2.0 mainnet
Stacks launches Proof of Transfer.
Smart contract chain anchored to Bitcoin.
Introduces Clarity smart contracts.

2021-11-14  Taproot activates
Taproot soft fork activates at block 709,632.
Introduces Schnorr signatures and script tree commitments.
Creates the infrastructure later used by inscription envelopes.

2022-12-14  First Ordinal inscription
Casey Rodarmor creates inscription 0 at block 767,430.
First widely recognized inscription embedded directly into a satoshi.

Cycle 2: Inscriptions, NFTs, and fungible tokens

2023-01-21  Ordinals launches
Casey Rodarmor releases ord v0.1.
Introduces sat numbering and inscription indexing.
Turns individual sats into uniquely traceable digital artifacts.

2023-03-08  BRC-20 launches
Domo publishes the BRC-20 experiment.
Simple JSON based fungible token standard using inscriptions.
At peak periods in 2023, BRC-20 related activity represented over half of Bitcoin transactions.

2023-04-15  Bitcoin Stamps (SRC-20)
Mike In Space launches Stamps.
Stores image data directly in spendable outputs.
Markets itself as highly permanent Bitcoin art storage.

2023-04-26  RGB protocol mainnet
RGB client side validation system launches.
Concept originally proposed years earlier.
Designed for scalable assets on Bitcoin and Lightning.

2023-06-05  Recursive inscriptions
ord v0.8 introduces recursive inscription support.
Inscriptions can reference other inscriptions.
Enables fully onchain generative art, games, and applications.
OCM Dimensions is one of the landmark examples.

2023-09-07  TAP protocol
BennyTheDev and the Trac ecosystem introduce TAP.
A more programmable evolution of BRC-20 with authorities, whitelist mints, redemptions, mass send, and Digital Matter Theory assets.
One of the first major attempts to push Bitcoin fungible tokens beyond simple JSON minting.

2023-09-22  Atomicals (ARC-20)
Atomicals Protocol launches.
Introduces UTXO native token ideas and Realm names.
Alternative approach to fungible tokens before Runes.

2023-10-09  BitVM paper
Robin Linus publishes the BitVM paper.
Proposes optimistic computation and Bitcoin verification schemes without requiring a soft fork.

2023-10-18  Taproot Assets
Lightning Labs launches Taproot Assets.
Bitcoin native asset protocol designed for Lightning integration.
Focused heavily on stablecoin and institutional payment use cases.

2023-12-15  PIPE protocol
Trac ecosystem launches PIPE.
UTXO-native fungible token design focused on reducing indexer complexity and improving scalability versus BRC-20.
Part of a broader push toward a Bitcoin-native OrdFi stack.

2023-12-17  Runestone airdrop
Leonidas distributes Runestone inscriptions.
One of the largest Bitcoin inscription airdrops.
Helps reignite Ordinals ecosystem activity.

2024-01-10  Spot Bitcoin ETFs approved
US regulators approve spot Bitcoin ETFs including BlackRock’s IBIT.
Massive institutional inflows reshape Bitcoin market structure.

2024-04-20  Runes activates
Casey Rodarmor launches Runes at the fourth Bitcoin halving.
UTXO native fungible token protocol built directly around Bitcoin transaction structure.

2024-05-01  Counterparty modernization
Counterparty ecosystem ships major modernization upgrades.
A reminder that one of Bitcoin’s earliest token protocols is still alive.

2024-08-22  Babylon Bitcoin staking
Babylon launches Bitcoin staking.
Allows BTC to help secure external systems without traditional bridging.

2024-08-26  Alkanes
Experimental smart contract layer associated with the Runes ecosystem.
Explores WASM style programmability for Bitcoin native assets.

2024-09-09  Fractal Bitcoin
UniSat launches Fractal Bitcoin.
Merge mined Bitcoin compatible sidechain with faster blocks.
Supports Bitcoin native asset experimentation.

2024-10-29  Stacks Nakamoto and sBTC
Stacks ships the Nakamoto upgrade.
sBTC launches later with a Bitcoin pegged asset model.
Major step toward a more active Bitcoin anchored smart contract economy.

2026-05-12  This week
Fungible token related activity represents a major share of Bitcoin transactions.
Bitcoin tokenization and asset issuance continue evolving more than 14 years after Colored Coins.

text:
原来 Codex 桌面端也能直接用 /goal，这玩意儿太香了

1. 先在终端里直接敲 `codex features enable goals`
2. 重启一下 Codex
3. 直接在聊天框开头打 `/goal` + 你的目标描述就行

目前桌面端 slash 菜单还没高亮显示 /goal，但可以直接用，启用后 goal 状态栏会自动跳出来

想让它真正用好 /goal，切记这几点：
1、目标一定要具体 + 可验证。比如：别写“帮我优化代码”，要写“把这个项目从 X 迁移到 Y，所有页面用 Playwright 测试保持视觉一致，测试通过率 100% 才算完成”。
2、用好子命令：`/goal pause` 暂停，`/goal resume` 继续，`/goal clear` 清掉当前任务，随时控场。
3、预算别忘控：长任务吃 token 猛，先在 config 里设上限。

text:
Our America 250 shirt celebrates the name of our country.. featuring Amerigo Vespucci!

Christopher Columbus first crossed the Atlantic in 1492 believing he had reached Asia. 

Just a few years later, between 1497 and 1504, Vespucci made his own voyages to the Americas and became one of the first explorers to argue that these lands were not Asia at all, but an entirely “new world.”

His writings spread rapidly across Europe, changing how people understood the globe itself.

In 1507, German cartographer Martin Waldseemüller published a map naming the newly recognized continents “America” in Vespucci’s honor. Using the Latin version of his name, “Americus,” he chose the feminine form “America.”

Live on the site now ♥️

Anthropic planned for 10x growth. They got 80x. Now they’re running on SpaceX GPUs, launching PE enterprise JVs, and sitting at $1.2 trillion.

Important!  Essential Oils for Ticks on Pets

I’ve seen a number of posts lately from people recommending different essential oils for tick prevention for pets.  

People, DO NOT put oils on your pets without checking to see if they are toxic. Pets are not people and react very differently to oils. 

Tea Tree Oil is highly toxic to pets.  Many others are toxic as well. 

Before you put any product on your pet, make sure it’s labeled for use in that species or check with a veterinarian before using. 

I’ve seen well meaning people have deadly consequences with essential oils and pets.

text:
New statements from Windward indicates that Iran still has about 23 days (at least) of on-vessel storage capacity until they hit tank tops. Combined with recent satellite imagery published by TankerTrackers showing available remaining storage on Kharg, Iran likely has ~30 days in total between onshore and on-vessel storage before approaching full capacity. 

Taking into account other measures Iran has taken to extend this timeline, including trucking routes into Pakistan, rail lines into China, and likely smuggling into Iraq, it is fair to assess that Iran has (at least) 35 days remaining. Utilizing historical “extreme measures” as a reference, where Saddam Hussein intentionally dumped around 10M barrels into the Gulf in the 1990’s, this would further add another 10 days to the timeline alone. To be clear… I do not advocate for such measures, but I’m operating in reality where if Iran truly risks “catastrophic” long-term damage, they would take emergency measures such as this to extend that timeline.

Best case scenario: ~35-45 days remaining. 

This is significant for a few reasons: 

1) Particularly egregious reporting from Fox News insinuated that Iran was intentionally dumping oil into the Gulf based on the satellite imagery of an oil slick near Kharg. There is conflicting reporting around the volume of this slick, with NYT stating 3,000 barrels, and other sources indicating 70,000 barrels. While this is not “environmentally” great, if Iran resorts to intentional dumping of oil into the Gulf, it’ll be measured in the millions of barrels… not the thousands. 

2) Satellite imagery shows the Iran has not loaded any oil onto vessels at Kharg over the past few days. Some have extrapolated this to conclude Iran has reached tank tops. Obviously, as can be derived from the statements made today by Windward, this is obviously not true. Iran has (at least) 23 days of available on-vessel storage remaining. 

3) Most importantly of all, this recent statement from Windward, combined with recently published satellite imagery from TankerTrackers of remaining onshore storage capacity on Kharg alone, it can be reasonably assessed that Iran has >30 days until shut-ins at the current production rate. This would bring the total timeline from imposition of blockade to shut-ins to 60 days. However, this is likely still optimistic, as emergency measures can likely extend this much further if necessary. 

4) Lastly, it is worth noting the key fundamental flaw inherent to the blockade and economic warfare theory: tactical success ≠ strategic success. 
Even IF Iran is forced to shut-in, that in and of itself is insufficient, and this is something Washington has largely failed to account for. Economic devastation for Iran is only beneficial insofar as it causes a toppling of the regime, or large concessions at the negotiating table. Economic devastation will not be equally distributed amongst the Iranian population. The wealthy and the elites will be hurt the least, and the average Iranian will be hurt the most. Unless this economic warfare campaign achieves one of these two strategic objectives, it will prove counterproductive to American’s long-term strategy.

Wisdom alone does not save the soul.

After death, the soul enters a world flooded with overwhelming spiritual wisdom — 
just as the earth is surrounded by air and nature, the dead are surrounded by cosmic intelligence.

But this wisdom is too vast to simply “receive.”

If the soul cannot transform it into living force, it becomes submerged in spirit itself.

Dr Steiner says that the task after death is to darken wisdom into life-force; to turn pure spiritual knowledge into something living, active, creative.

And this requires something far deeper than intellect:

inner strength, moral power, creative spiritual activity,..

Otherwise the soul is “drowned in spirit.”

The spiritual world is not passive contemplation.
It is creation.

“The important thing in the spiritual world is that we should have the impulse, the power, to make something out of this wisdom, to produce from it reality.”

And this is exactly where Christ enters the picture.

Steiner is very clear: Christ is not a mere teacher or symbol - Christ is the Living Divine Being at the center of Earth evolution.  

Philosophy can reach the Father-God, the realm of order, causality, cosmic law.

But Christ cannot be reached through logic alone.

Why?

Because Christ is not an abstract idea.

Christ is a real divine Being, the Sun-Spirit, who must be recognized inwardly through freedom, faith, moral awakening, or spiritual perception.

This is why Steiner says Christ “proves Himself” only through spiritual knowledge.

Christ awakens the exact force the soul needs after death:
the ability to remain awake, individual, and creative within the ocean of cosmic wisdom.

Without this force, the human “I” risks dissolving into spiritual vastness.

With Christ, the soul remains itself while expanding into the cosmos.

“We provide ourselves with the right impulses to pass through the portal of death when we find the true relationship to Christ.”

And also:

“God the Father we can find during life; we find the Christ when we understand dying in the right way.”

“In Christo Morimur” — In Christ we die.

Not as defeat => but as passage.
Christ is the guide through the threshold.

The Being who:
- meets the soul after death
- carries it through the Midnight Hour
- prevents it from being overwhelmed by spiritual forces
- helps transform cosmic wisdom into the life-forces needed for rebirth

There are two dangers after death:

1. Being drowned in spirit
— losing oneself in overwhelming cosmic wisdom.

2. Being hardened in matter
— losing the capacity to transform spirit into living creative force.

Christ stands between both extremes.

He keeps the soul: awake, free, individualized, morally upright,..

The strongest souls are not the ones who know the most; but the ones who can transform wisdom into living reality.

text:
Eventually, the Party comes to a Close. The story lives on though, here's why....

When I first saw this car come up on Bring a Trailer (BaT) the other day, there was a hint of memory I had seen it before and a shared connection. It didn't really gel until a day later why I was attracted to it, so let's dive into the rest of that story. 

Back in the 1970's, Ronnie Montrose was one of those iconic guitarists in Rock that raised the bar with his talent and musicality. I had the Montrose cassette tapes and albums that played over and over again. Sammy Hagar joined on the debut of the album "Montrose" in 1973 that was formed by Ronnie after he left the Edgar Winter Group. That was followed by "Paper Money"  in 1974, another great album that expressed the talents of Ronnie and Sammy.  The entirety of those two albums alone were part of my teenage years, with music that becomes part of your soul guided by the lyrics.

Last year this car came up at the Barrett-Jackson Auction in Scottsdale. It is told the car was built originally for Ronnie and the band, which Sammy later bought from Ronnie at some point. The auction proceeds were then given to a charitable cause for Suicide Prevention, which is a hat-tip and honorarium to Ronnie who committed suicide in 2012 at 64 years old. 

I mentioned earlier the shared connection, so here it is; Ronnie's suicide became a subliminal turning point for me to face my own reality with a lifelong diagnosis of biological depression. After decades of varietal treatments that failed, battles with alcohol, drugs and other addictive behaviors that ended prior relationships, jobs and huge personal relationship strain, it became time to face and fix the problem. 

This began a multi-year journey of discovery, testing, lots of science including DNA analysis, brain scans and anything else I could find to get to the Root of the issue. The answer became more obvious when it was discovered that I had a minor "dead spot" for lack of a better term in the Pre-Frontal Cortex of my brain that was a core driver to the depression I had been battling my entire life. This along with a chemical deficiency discovered through DNA and blood analysis was the reason I had suffered. So we started with an experimental treatment called rTMS (Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation), a cousin to the more severe Electroshock therapy, and my entire world began to change for the better. After several years of treatments, chemical rebalancing that didn't involve drug therapy, I was essentially cured and remain so to this day. 

Now I told you all of that to share this; The car I bid on, the 1962 Thunderbird on Bring a Trailer, became sort of a tribute to that struggle, and one in which Ronnie paid the ultimate price for with his life. I wanted the car not only because it's a bitchen Sled or some flex, but, to have and share it as the honorarium to the struggle which many still face today. And so I'm writing about it here and in the book I've been working on the past 10 years about that topic and my personal struggle overcoming lifelong depression. I hope to share that with you all soon as well. The car is also my birth year, and now at 64 myself (same age Ronnie took his life), the coincidences and mission at hand seemed obvious, so I bid on the car. 

For the today and now, I'm out of the Bidding War for this Car on BaT as it's going North of my Retirement Budget reality. I'm hoping the car will bring another Bidder joy and remembrance to the legend Ronnie left behind.  

Thanks for reading & being a part of the journey with me...

Other Closely Related Energy Storage Plays

text:
The biggest flaw in how we train frontier AI models is embarrassingly simple. 

Imagine spending a full day solving a hard problem. You try dozens of approaches, hit dead ends, backtrack, get lucky once. Your model reasons for hundreds of steps. But, at the very end, it gets one signal: right or wrong.

That single bit gets broadcast across the entire chain as if every step contributed equally. Wrong turns get reinforced because the answer landed. Good reasoning gets penalized because the conclusion missed.

It's not a subtle flaw. It's a fundamental misattribution of credit. But, this is we train the most capable AI systems on earth.

It's like sucking supervision through a straw.

Our spending data continues to show the consumer holding up overall, but cracks are beginning to emerge beneath the surface.

Our latest analysis shows Apparel, Accessories & Footwear as one of the clearest areas of softness, with Footwear/Athletic Apparel seeing the sharpest deceleration vs. late February. 

Travel trends have softened as well. Airline growth remains positive, but the acceleration appears driven entirely by average transaction size growth, while Cruises and Lodging have both decelerated.

The table below highlights where spending momentum has recently weakened…and where resilience continues to hold.
